verdict_reason: The exponentiated mean-NLL path agrees with independent Hugging Face accounting to 2.8e-6 relative, but bits_per_byte does not always divide by the bytes corresponding to scored source text. With an automatically prepended BOS that decodes to '<BOS>', a ten-byte stream at exactly one bit per source byte returns 2.000000005 instead of 1.000000003; the correct denominator is all ten source bytes because BOS consumed none.
comparable_reason: Token PPL is tokenizer-dependent by definition, and the rare/frequent buckets use a different model-specific alphabet. On the same effective corpus, PPL was 34.9899, 33.4086, 21.8046, and 21.0207 for Pythia-70M, DistilGPT2, GPT-2, and Pythia-160M, respectively (Spearman rho=-1.0 with parameter count, n=4); bits_per_byte reduced tokenizer dependence but still had rho=-0.8 and retains the BOS denominator error.
github_reason: Fetched the official Transformers fixed-length-PPL procedure and ran it head-to-head with current strided_perplexity on GPT-2 over the full WikiText-2-raw test stream. BLME gave 25.1702909 versus 25.1702210 for the guide loop (relative error 2.78e-6); BLME counted the actual 287,643 shifted labels, while the guide's blanket minus-one-per-pass accounting counted 287,083.
paper_reason: Radford et al. report GPT-2 117M WikiText-2 PPL 29.41. Current BLME's full-raw 1024/512 result is 25.17029 (14.42% lower), while changing only to disjoint 1024-token blocks gives 29.94031 (1.803% higher); the shipped filtered WikiText-103 slice gives 21.8046 and has no published counterpart.
confounds_reason: The same-text four-model sweep gives rho=-1.0 between ppl_overall and parameter count and rho=-0.8 for bits_per_byte. Separately, study-v3 raw PPL has rho=-0.768 with d_model, -0.637 with n_layers, and -0.528 with vocab_size (n=45), so the task is predominantly a likelihood/scale control rather than beyond-scale evidence.
defects: CODE src/blme/tasks/geometry/utils.py:533-539: subtracting decode(first_id) from source bytes assumes the first ID consumed those bytes; automatically inserted BOS/control tokens violate that assumption and doubled BPB in the ten-byte closed form.

CODE src/blme/tasks/geometry/utils.py:465-505: stride is allowed to equal max_length, but each later chunk then lacks the one-token overlap required by the model's internal shift; a 10-token stream with max_length=stride=4 scored 7 rather than all 9 predictable targets.

CODE src/blme/tasks/geometry/perplexity.py:45-60: frequency ties are broken by token ID. On the effective GPT-2 corpus, 1,799 of 3,121 observed types were hapax; selecting the tied rare types by ID gave rare PPL 115.74 versus 301.84 on average after semantics-preserving random tie orders.

CODE src/blme/tasks/geometry/perplexity.py:98-128: any strided-pass exception silently changes the advertised ppl_overall estimand to per-document PPL, with no returned protocol/window/stride flag; the measured GPT-2 change is about 74% (21.80 to 37.91).

CONFIG src/blme/tasks/configs/defaults.yaml:79-80 plus src/blme/cache.py:454-491: the effective num_samples is 100 and load_default_corpus filters out every row shorter than 50 before taking the leading rows, so the output called WikiText-103 perplexity is neither the full nor verbatim validation split.

COMPARABILITY: raw token PPL and the model-specific rare/frequent partitions are not defined on a common token alphabet; bits_per_byte is the right explicit cross-tokenizer family but does not remove the measured scale dependence.
fix: Use tokenizer offsets or an explicit source-span map so BPB counts exactly the bytes represented by scored non-control tokens; never subtract decoded special-token spellings. Require 0 < stride < max_length or start every disjoint chunk one token earlier, fail closed instead of silently changing protocols, emit achieved protocol/window/stride metadata, and include all count-boundary ties (or define occurrence quantiles) rather than selecting tied types by token ID. In configuration, use an immutable full raw split when naming a WikiText result and record its digest.
